ops.text:
ccx vcs ship hangs after staging, silently dropping the prek lint gate

Observed 2026-08-28 while shipping v0.47.0 from /Users/yasyf/Code/cc-context on the plain-git lane (no jj, no Graphite; `ccx vcs info` reported lane=git, branch=main, trunk=main, permission=ADMIN).

`ccx vcs ship -m '<msg>' <6 paths>` staged all six files (git status showed 5 M, 1 A) and then hung before creating the commit. After ~7 minutes:
- STAT=S, 0.0% CPU, no CPU accumulation
- no child processes
- no open network sockets (`lsof -p <pid> -a -i` empty)
- no .git/index.lock
- stdin /dev/null, stdout/stderr pipes open

It never recovered. I killed it and completed the commit and push by hand. The tree was left correctly staged, so the hang sits between staging and commit.

Second-order consequence, and the more damaging one: prek is NOT installed as a git hook in this checkout (no .git/hooks/pre-commit) — ship invokes `uvx prek` itself. So a ship that dies after staging means a hand-finished commit runs no lint at all. That is what happened: two gosec G115 findings in internal/semsearch/rank/bm25.go reached CI and turned the run red on a commit that would otherwise have been gated locally.

Two separable issues:
1. The hang itself.
2. A ship that fails partway leaves the tree staged with no signal that the lint gate was skipped, so a hand-finished commit bypasses linting silently.

Also found while diagnosing: `uvx prek run` cannot run golangci-lint in this checkout at all — it pins GOTOOLCHAIN=local with go 1.26.5 while go.mod requires >= 1.26.6, so the hook errors with "context loading failed: failed to load packages". Even an explicit local prek run would not have caught the gosec findings.
